label: Map it to the stack
prompt: Assign each technology or concept to its correct layer in a full-stack web application.

items.explanation: React components are frontend — they run in the browser but represent the application logic layer above raw HTML. 'Frontend' and 'Browser' are distinct: frontend is the code you write; browser is the runtime that executes it.
SQL runs inside the database engine and never leaves that layer. The backend calls it, but the JOIN itself executes in the database.
Express handlers run on the Node.js server process — not in the browser, not in the database.
localStorage is a browser API that stores data in the user's own browser. It's not accessible from the server and disappears if the user clears their data.
Token verification must happen server-side. If you only verified it in the browser, any user could trivially bypass it by editing JavaScript.
CSS is part of the frontend presentation layer. It's sent to the browser as a file and interpreted by the rendering engine — but it's code you write on the frontend.
Indexes are a database-layer optimization — they exist entirely inside the database engine and speed up query lookups.
fetch() is called from JavaScript running in the browser (your frontend code) to make an HTTP request to the backend API.
